title: When an Unbeliever Fears God More

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Early the next morning Abimelek summoned all his officials, and when he told them all that had happened, they were very much afraid. Then Abimelek called Abraham in and said, "What have you done to us? How have I wronged you that you have brought such great guilt upon me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that should never be done." - Gen 20:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There is a painful role-reversal in this scene. Abimelech, the pagan king, responds to God's warning with immediate action and reverent fear - he rises "early the next morning," gathers his officials, and they are "very much afraid." Meanwhile Abraham, the man of God, stands silent, exposed, with nothing to say for himself. The unbeliever fears God more than the believer did.

This is humbling to read. Abimelech's rebuke is entirely just: "You have done things to me that should never be done." A pagan king lectures God's chosen servant on right and wrong - and he is correct. Abraham has no defence. His compromise has brought guilt not only on himself but on a whole kingdom.

It is a sobering reminder that God's people can, in a given moment, live worse than those who don't know Him. Our position as believers is no guarantee that our conduct will honour God. Sometimes the world rightly calls us out, and we deserve it.

Rather than making us defensive, this should make us humble. When an unbeliever's conduct or conscience shames our own, the right response is not to bristle but to repent. And it should sharpen our witness - for the watching world does notice when those who claim to follow God fail to live it. "Live such good lives among the pagans that... they may see your good deeds and glorify God" (1 Pet 2:12). Let your life match your faith.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Has your conduct ever been rightly rebuked by someone outside the faith?
- Does your life match the faith you profess?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, humble me when my conduct falls short of my faith. Give me a soft heart to receive correction, even from unexpected sources, and help me live a life that honours You before a watching world.
Amen.
